summary: Specifies the Link Management Protocol, which runs between a pair of nodes to manage traffic engineering links. Multiple data links can be combined into a single TE link, and management can use out-of-band techniques. It is a standards-track document.

eli5.summary: Neighbors check that the wires between them work and agree on what each is for. LMP is the conversation they use to do that.

questions: how does lmp verify data links
subtitle: How two neighboring network nodes keep their control channels alive, check their links and report faults.

tldr.problem: When many physical links between two nodes are grouped into one traffic engineering link, and control messages may travel on a different path than user data, each side needs a way to check that the control path works, that the links really connect, and that both sides describe them the same way.
tldr.mechanism: LMP runs over UDP between neighbors. It negotiates and monitors control channels with Config and Hello messages, compares link properties with LinkSummary, tests each data link with Test messages, and reports failures with ChannelStatus messages.
tldr.outcome: It gives a GMPLS control plane one protocol for control channel health, link property agreement, link verification and fault localization. It is a Proposed Standard and was later updated by RFC 6898.

facts.label: Required security
facts.value: IPsec ESP in tunnel mode; IKE for dynamic keys

today: RFC 4204 is a Proposed Standard published in October 2005, and the metadata shows it has not been obsoleted. It has been updated by RFC 6898. Its SONET/SDH test message encoding is described in RFC 4207.

sections.title: Why Link Management Is Needed
sections.content:
RFC 4204 defines the Link Management Protocol (LMP). It runs between a pair of neighboring nodes in networks that use a common control plane such as Generalized MPLS (GMPLS). A pair of nodes may have thousands of interconnects, so for scalability several data links can be combined into a single traffic engineering (TE) link.

Control messages need a control channel, which the RFC defines as a pair of mutually reachable IP interfaces. In GMPLS the control channel does not have to use the same physical medium as the data links. It could be a separate wavelength, fiber, Ethernet link, an IP tunnel or a multi-hop IP network. The consequence is that the health of the control channel does not necessarily say anything about the health of the data links, and the reverse. The fate of the two must be handled separately.

LMP covers four jobs: maintaining control channel connectivity, correlating link properties, verifying the physical connectivity of data links, and managing faults. The first two are core procedures. Link verification and fault management are optional. LMP also acts as glue in the control plane: it can hand link properties to the routing module and tell the signaling module how TE links map to control channels.

The RFC also distinguishes ports from component links. Component links are multiplex capable and ports are not, and that changes how resources are allocated and verified.
sections.eli5: Imagine two houses joined by lots of garden hoses, plus a separate telephone line. A hose can burst while the phone still works, and the phone can break while the water still flows. LMP lets the neighbors watch both.

sections.title: Control Channels and the Hello Protocol
sections.content:
Each node gives every control channel a node-wide unique, non-zero 32-bit identifier, the CC_Id. All LMP packets run over UDP using the LMP port number, so the link-level encoding of the control channel is outside the scope of the RFC. Several control channels can be active at once, and their parameters MUST be negotiated individually.

A channel is activated by a Config message that must be answered by a ConfigAck. If the receiver disagrees it sends a ConfigNack, which flags unacceptable non-negotiable objects and proposes alternatives for negotiable ones. Objects carry an N bit that marks them negotiable or not. If both nodes send Config at the same time, the node with the higher Node_Id wins and the other stops sending Config and answers. Equal Node_Ids mean misconfiguration. To learn the far end address, a Config may be sent to the multicast address 224.0.0.1 or ff02::1.

Once configured, the Hello protocol is a lightweight keep-alive. The nodes agree on a HelloInterval and a HelloDeadInterval, both in milliseconds. The dead interval MUST be greater than the interval and SHOULD be at least 3 times as large. For a directly connected link the suggested defaults are 150 ms and 500 ms. If the fast keep-alive is not used, both values MUST be zero.

Each Hello carries two sequence numbers: TxSeqNum for this Hello and RcvSeqNum for the last Hello received. TxSeqNum is never 0, and 1 means the sender just started or restarted. After (2^32)-1 the next value is 2. A control channel moves to the up state once a node has sent a Hello and received a valid one.

A channel can be taken down gracefully with the ControlChannelDown flag in the common header. If every control channel is lost while data links still carry user traffic, the TE link is in a Degraded state, and routing and signaling SHOULD be told so that new connections are not accepted.
sections.eli5: The neighbors keep saying "are you there?" and "yes, I heard number 5" on the phone. If the answers stop for too long, they decide the phone line is dead.

sections.title: Link Property Correlation and Link Verification
sections.content:
Link property correlation uses the LinkSummary, LinkSummaryAck and LinkSummaryNack messages. A LinkSummary holds a TE_LINK object, which gives the local and remote Link_Id and says whether fault management and link verification are supported, followed by one or more DATA_LINK objects with the local and remote Interface_Ids. Identifiers must be of the same type (IPv4, IPv6 or unnumbered) at both ends, otherwise a Nack is returned. The exchange SHOULD happen before a link is brought up.

Link verification is optional. It checks the physical connectivity of data links and can discover which interface at one end is wired to which at the other. It SHOULD be done when a TE link is set up and periodically for unallocated data links. Because transparent devices normally do not look at the data, the links must become opaque until they are allocated to user traffic.

The initiator sends BeginVerify over the control channel. The remote node answers with BeginVerifyAck and a 32-bit node-unique Verify_Id. The initiator then sends periodic Test messages on each data link, the only LMP message sent over a data link. The receiver replies on the control channel with TestStatusSuccess or TestStatusFailure, which the sender confirms with TestStatusAck. When all links are tested, EndVerify and EndVerifyAck close the procedure.
sections.eli5: To find out which hose goes where, one neighbor sends a little splash of colored water down each hose and says over the phone "watch hose 1". The other neighbor says which of his taps got wet.

sections.title: Fault Management
sections.content:
Fault management is also optional, and its use is negotiated in the LinkSummary exchange. With transparent devices, fault detection moves to the physical layer, such as loss of light. LMP does not care how a failure is detected, only that it is.

When a link fails, nodes further downstream may all notice it, which would cause a storm of alarms. To localize the fault, a downstream node that sees a failure sends a ChannelStatus message to its upstream neighbor, bundling all failed data links. The upstream node MUST answer with ChannelStatusAck and checks whether the failure is also visible at its own input. If it is not, the upstream node has localized the failure to the link between them. If no status arrives, a node SHOULD send ChannelStatusRequest, and the answer comes back as ChannelStatusResponse.

The CHANNEL_STATUS object carries an Active bit, a Direction bit and a status of Signal Okay (1), Signal Degrade (2) or Signal Fail (3). To report a whole TE link as failed, the object holds a single Interface_Id of zero. The same message can also tell a neighbor to start or stop actively monitoring a data link, called channel activation and deactivation indication.
sections.eli5: When a pipe breaks, every house down the street notices the water stopped. Each one tells the house before it, and the last one that still has water knows the break is just past it.

sections.title: Reliable Messages, Restart and Addressing
sections.content:
LMP builds its own reliability. Messages carry a MESSAGE_ID that must increase monotonically, and the matching MESSAGE_ID_ACK repeats it. Control channel messages are scoped to the CC_Id and TE link messages to the LMP adjacency. Out-of-order messages are dropped as the RFC describes for Config, LinkSummary and ChannelStatus. Unacknowledged messages SHOULD be retransmitted using an exponential back-off. The suggested defaults are an initial interval of 500 ms, a power of 2 back-off (Delta = 1) and a retry limit of 3.

For graceful restart, a node that lost its LMP state sets the LMP Restart flag in its messages until a Hello arrives whose RcvSeqNum equals its own TxSeqNum. The neighbor then sends a LinkSummary for each TE link with all objects non-negotiable, so the restarted node can recover link mappings and learn which data links are allocated. Afterwards the restarted node SHOULD send ChannelStatusRequest and verify unallocated data channels.

All messages, except in some cases Test, use UDP port 701. Config messages SHOULD go to the multicast address on a point-to-point link, and otherwise MUST go to an IP address on the neighboring node.
sections.eli5: Every message gets a number, like numbered letters. If no reply comes, you resend, waiting longer each time. If one neighbor forgets everything after a power cut, the other helps him remember.

sections.title: The Three State Machines
sections.content:
The RFC defines finite state machines for control channels, TE links and data links.

A control channel starts in Down, moves through the negotiation states ConfSnd (sending Config) or ConfRcv (waiting for one), then Active (exchanging Hellos), and reaches Up when a valid Hello arrives. GoingDown covers administrative shutdown. Seventeen numbered events drive it, such as evBringUp, evConfDone and evHoldTimer.

A TE link is Down with no data links, Init while LinkSummary is being synchronized, Up in normal operation, or Degraded when all control channels are down but some data links still carry traffic.

A data link is Down, Test (sending Test messages), PasvTest (listening for them), Up/Free or Up/Alloc. Separate diagrams exist for the active (sending) and passive (receiving) side.
sections.eli5: Each wire and each phone line is like a traffic light with a few colors. The rules say which color can change to which, and what has to happen first.

sections.title: Message and Object Formats
sections.content:
Every LMP message starts with a common header and then a sequence of objects. The header holds a 4-bit version (this is version 1), flags, an 8-bit message type and a 16-bit length. Two flags are defined: 0x01 ControlChannelDown and 0x02 LMP Restart. All values are in network byte order.

Each object has a header with the N bit (negotiable or not), a 7-bit C-Type, an 8-bit Class and a 16-bit Length. The RFC defines object classes such as CCID, NODE_ID, LINK_ID, INTERFACE_ID, MESSAGE_ID, CONFIG, HELLO, BEGIN_VERIFY, TE_LINK, DATA_LINK, CHANNEL_STATUS and ERROR_CODE. Message grammars use notation such as <Hello Message> ::= <Common Header> <LOCAL_CCID> <HELLO>, and the listed transmission order SHOULD be followed.

Nack messages use ERROR_CODE objects whose bits can be combined. For BeginVerifyNack, for example, 0x01 means link verification is not supported and 0x02 means the node is unwilling to verify, in which case the initiator SHOULD retry after Rf seconds.
sections.eli5: Every message has an envelope with the same boxes in the same places. Inside are smaller labelled boxes, so the other side always knows what is what.

sections.title: Security With IPsec
sections.content:
The RFC lists attacks such as spoofed, modified or replayed control packets, and attempts to break the key. It requires that LMP security provide authentication, integrity and replay protection. Confidentiality is not needed for LMP control traffic, and Test packets on data links need no protection.

Where security is needed, implementations are told to use IPsec. ESP with trailer authentication in tunnel mode MUST be supported, and IKE MUST be used when keys are negotiated dynamically. Manual keying SHOULD be supported but is recommended only for diagnostics, as it cannot provide replay protection or automatic re-keying. The IKE identities MUST be IP addresses, and the protocol field MUST be UDP.

If IPsec is configured for a peer, a receiver should reject LMP traffic that does not arrive through the crypto channel. Because a Hello failure may also be a crypto channel failure, the RFC recommends tearing down and re-establishing both when all control channels fail. For dynamically discovered peers it recommends digital signatures over pre-shared keys, and it strongly discourages one shared secret among many peers.
sections.eli5: To stop a stranger from faking the neighbors' phone calls, they use a secret handshake so each knows the other is really who they say.
